text:
aisha: Quick postmortem follow-up from last night's outage — we had a cloud region flake, model-registry read timeouts, and OIDC token refresh errors. Need concrete owners + timelines for mitigations. I'll compile AIs here. Please respond with ownership or :wave: if you can't take.
incidents-bot: Postmortem doc: https://redwood.internal/notes/PM-2026-03-22-vendor-chain (summary pinned). Runbooks: /runbooks/model-registry-failover, /runbooks/auth-provider-degrad.
ben: I'll own cloud failover automation. Plan: add automated region failover policy for critical routes + health-check gating. ETA: 2026-04-07. Will open PR for the policy and add smoke tests.
carlos: I'll take model registry mitigations — implement read-replicas, client-side retries with circuit breaker, and a lightweight local cache for model metadata. ETA: 2026-04-12. I'll coordinate with eng-ml for cache TTLs.
lucy: For model-registry fallback, we should also add a mode where serving pins to a cached manifest when registry is unreachable for >30s. I'll sketch the impl and tests. ETA: 2026-04-05. Note: this is a recurring issue — similar symptoms in Dec and Feb.
marco: On the auth side, we saw token refresh race causing 401 storms. Proposal: centralize refresh logic into a single refreshed-token service with attestation to reduce burst. I'll draft threat/perm changes. ETA: 2026-04-15.
eve: Product note — prioritize the model-registry cached-manifest and cloud failover in the next sprint for customers on Dedicated. Please tag the customer-impacting items so I can escalate in roadmap.
kevin: Ops will add region-level capacity alarms and an automated pager for partial-region degradations. Also recommend we test cross-region failover monthly. I'll create a runbook test ticket. ETA: 2026-04-02.
ben: Quick detail — for region failover: do we want automated DNS switch or application-layer routing? I prefer application-layer routing with sticky session awareness.
aisha: Good question. Let's go app-layer first (safer). Ben, add a toggle in the policy to enable DNS switch if app-layer fails after N minutes.
carlos: Action item list (I'll create tracking tickets):
- AI-611: Cloud app-layer failover + smoke tests (owner: ben) ETA: 2026-04-07
- AI-612: Model-registry read-replicas + retries (owner: carlos) ETA: 2026-04-12
- AI-613: Serving cached-manifest fallback (owner: lucy) ETA: 2026-04-05
- AI-614: Centralized token refresh service + perms (owner: marco) ETA: 2026-04-15
- AI-615: Region capacity alarms + monthly failover test (owner: kevin) ETA: 2026-04-02
incidents-bot: Tickets created: AI-611, AI-612, AI-613, AI-614, AI-615. Linked to PM-2026-03-22.
lucy: Note on recurrence — model registry errors showed two escalation patterns: (1) increased read latency under metadata churn, (2) auth 401 storms that made retries worse. We should treat them as linked: retries + 401s can amplify load.
marco: Agree. Also propose short-term mitigation: add jittered backoff and limit concurrent refreshes per instance to 1. We'll push that as a hotfix next 48h if someone signs off.
ben: I can review and sign off for hotfix. Ben -> hotfix branch with throttled refresh and jittered backoff. If it helps, link sample snippet:```python
# simplified token refresh guard
if not token_refresh_in_progress:
    token_refresh_in_progress = True
    try:
        refresh_token()
    finally:
        token_refresh_in_progress = False
```
kevin: Ops will stage the hotfix in canary tomorrow and watch token error rate + 5xxs. Please add a short test plan in the PR.
carlos: I'll also add a client-side circuit breaker to avoid hammering registry during auth storms. Small PR by EOD tomorrow.
aisha: Thanks all — two asks before I close the loop: 1) update the ticket with concrete test plans and rollout steps, 2) add rollback criteria and monitoring alerts tied to the ai tickets. I'll re-run the recurring-incident analysis next week and propose permanent cadence (quarterly vs monthly) for these vendor-dependency drills.
eve: I'll ensure customer-impacting items are tagged and prioritized for Dedicated customers. If timelines slip, I'll coordinate a mitigation comms plan.
ben: Quick doc pointers: smoke tests -> https://redwood.internal/tests/failover-smoke and model registry runbook -> /runbooks/model-registry-failover (already linked by bot).
incidents-bot: Reminder: postmortem follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-28 10:00 PT. Calendar invite sent to participants.
aisha: OK I'll mark my list complete when PRs are open and tests are passing. If anyone can't meet ETA, update AI ticket with proposed new ETA within 24h. Closing thread soon but keep updates on the AI tickets.
kevin: Noted. Will post canary results in AI-611.
lucy: Posting quick addendum: I'll include a small eval harness to verify fidelity of cached-manifest vs live-registry to avoid model mismatch regressions.
marco: And I'll list the minimal IAM changes required for the token-service in AI-614.
ben: 👍
aisha: Thanks — appreciate the quick turn.
